text: Adult Ascaris live in the pig intestine for up to a year, laying over 500,000 eggs, which are very resistant in the environment. Piglets pick up eggs shed by the mother that stick to the udder skin — pregnant sows act as the main reservoir — so it's important to de-worm sows before farrowing and wash them with soap (especially around the anus and udder) before they enter the farrowing pen. Treat/prevent Ascaris and other roundworms with Ivermectin 1% (1 ml/30 kg) or Levamisole 7.5% (1 ml/10 kg): sows should be treated 2 weeks before farrowing, and piglets 1 week after weaning. There is no treatment for Trichinella — the only real safeguard is cooking pork thoroughly before eating it.
